fire: The bishop sat on a carved throne, called a cathedra, in the choir.

The pointed arches of the nave rest on carved column capitals.
A cathedral takes its name from the seat of the bishop, the cathedra.
Medieval masons built the choir, the ambulatory and the flying buttresses.
The abbey church has a Romanesque nave and a vaulted crypt.
The rose window above the transept fills the church with colour.
quiet: The mayor sat on a plastic chair, called a stool, in the hall.

The steel beams of the garage rest on poured concrete blocks.
A hotel takes its name from the street of the city, the avenue.
Modern builders put up the offices, the car park and the loading docks.
The office tower has a marble lobby and a heated pool.
The large window above the entrance fills the store with light.
